english: Let $ABC$ be a triangle in which $\angle C=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Then the maximum value of $7\sin A+8\sin B$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $ABC$ एक त्रिभुज है जिसमें $\angle C=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ है। तब $7\sin A+8\sin B$ का अधिकतम मान ______ है।
solution: Maximum at $\tan A=\dfrac{11}{4\sqrt3}$, i.e. $A\approx57.8^\circ\in\left(0^\circ,120^\circ\right)$, so it is attained: maximum $=13$
solution_full: So $7\sin A+8\sin B=11\sin A+4\sqrt3\cos A=13\sin(A+\phi)$, where $\cos\phi=\dfrac{11}{13}$, $\sin\phi=\dfrac{4\sqrt3}{13}$.

The value $13$ needs $A+\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, i.e. $\tan A=\cot\phi=\dfrac{11}{4\sqrt3}\approx1.588$, $A\approx57.8^\circ$, $B\approx62.2^\circ$. This lies in the allowed range, so the maximum $13$ is attained.
originality_note: New: weights 7 and 8 with the 60 degree constraint give the amplitude sqrt(7^2 + 8^2 + 7*8) = 13 (way 5); the attainment inside the triangle must be checked. Closest known: max of sin A + sin B + sin C, or max of a sin A + b sin B for a right angle C. Different because: the 60 degree constraint makes the cross term +ab, and the maximiser must lie in (0, 120 degrees).

concept_use.Range of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x); maximum an: 11 sin A + 4 sqrt3 cos A has maximum sqrt(121 + 48) = 13.
